title: Wall Street's AI sell-off: the Nasdaq falls 5.5% two days after the midterms
seoTitle: Why US stocks fell: the AI sell-off explained
dek: The S&P 500 had its worst day since April 2025 on 5 November as AI and chip stocks fell. President Trump blames Democrats; analysts point to the election, borrowing costs and hedge funds locking in profits.
happened: On Thursday 5 November the S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73, the Dow lost 1,833 points, or 3.44%, to 51,523.06, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to 24,315, its worst day since April 2025 and into correction territory. Chip stocks led the fall: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost about 12%, Nvidia about 9.3% and AMD 17.3%. The drop followed the market's best day in three months on 4 November, the day after the election. On Friday morning South Korea's Kospi fell more than 8% and Japan's Nikkei about 6%, London's FTSE 100 was down 1.9% by mid-morning, and US Nasdaq futures pointed about 1.3% higher before the open.

sides.says: He posted on Truth Social that the market "suffered one of the Worst Days in History based on the results of the Election" and said: "Your 401(k)s have, therefore, dropped. Remember, it wasn't Republicans, it was Dumocrats."

sides.who: Analysts who point to the election
sides.says: Jakub Rochlitz of eToro said: "The obvious catalyst for the sharp selloff is that markets are pricing in the midterm results", and that investors expect the AI buildout to "become slower and more expensive". AP reports that the wins raised the possibility of government-imposed pauses in data centre construction, amid voter concern about power bills.

Charlie McElligott of Nomura said the main catalyst was hedge funds locking in profits before year-end, not a fundamental deterioration. AP also cites worries about higher borrowing costs and critics who say AI stock prices form a bubble.
AMD chief executive Lisa Su said "the market can sometimes be a little bit short-sighted" and that she does not see demand for AI chips slowing soon.
NBC News reports that many incoming Democrats have backed slowing or halting data centre construction. The reports read here carried no direct Democratic response to the sell-off or to Trump's post.

next: Fox Business reports that many analysts said the selling could continue. Friday's US close was not yet known when this was last checked, and premarket prices can change at the open. Yahoo Finance reports that Brent crude traded near $98 on 5 November amid uncertainty over a US deal with Iran.
summary: US stocks had their sharpest fall since April 2025 on 5 November, led by AI and chip companies, and markets in Asia and Europe fell on 6 November. The reasons are disputed. President Trump blames the Democrats' midterm wins. Some analysts agree the election played a part, because Democrats may restrict data centres; others say hedge funds taking profits and higher borrowing costs mattered more. The fall came a day after the market's best day in three months.
